source.title: Co-Supervised Learning: Improving Weak-to-Strong Generalization with Hierarchical Mixture of Experts

page_placements.theme: Multiple weak supervisors: assignment, weighting, boosting, merging and diversity

record.tranche_reason: The study measures performance gap recovery in visual weak-to-strong fine-tuning and compares co-supervision with a vanilla single-supervisor baseline. Its experiments use a different, vision-focused setting and add multiple specialized supervisors and denoising.
record.gate_note: The paper reports PGR results in Figures 2, 7 and 8; plotted values are not transcribed numerically in the text, so those row values are recorded as figure only. Figure 6 reports collective supervisor accuracy and teacher-assignment capability, not student PGR, and is not included as a row.
record.test_reason: The study re-runs the original's vision protocol: an AlexNet weak supervisor and a DINO ViT student with linear heads, measured by PGR. Figure 2 sweeps supervisor capability under vanilla weak-to-strong training. Figures 7–8 compare a new multi-supervisor training method plus denoising against the vanilla single-supervisor baseline on ImageNet and DomainNet. These results bear directly on V1, V2, V3 and V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Hierarchical co-supervision with specialized weak teachers plus teacher-student and local-global consistency denoising beats the vanilla single-supervisor baseline on two vision datasets. Generality beyond vision recognition is unknown. The paraphrase should add that the authors show vanilla weak-to-strong PGR shrinks as the capability gap widens, which motivates the method.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the weak-to-strong fine-tuning setup and PGR measure in visual recognition with pre-trained encoders and linear classifiers. The proposed approach adds multiple specialized supervisors, iterative teacher assignment and denoising; the paper also reports a vanilla single-supervisor baseline.
record.method_sensitivity: PGR varies with weak-supervisor capability; results also vary across dataset, number of specialized supervisors, label format (hard or soft), and whether denoising is applied.

fits_no_version.finding: Collective accuracy of specialized weak supervisors rises over 0.05 per doubling of supervisor count. The student-guided teacher assignment captures about 2/3 of the oracle gain (Figure 6). This is supervisor accuracy, not student PGR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Student-guided assignment among specialized weak supervisors recovers much of the oracle collective-supervisor accuracy.

record.problems: The study is limited to visual recognition and explicitly says transfer to language understanding, generative modeling and reward modeling is unclear. PGR values in the figures are not given numerically in the text; results are averaged across three random seeds, but no error bars or other uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 6's collective supervisor accuracy and teacher-assignment capability results are omitted because they do not measure student PGR or the student beating its supervisor. Figure 2's plotted values are retained as one capability-sweep row because the text describes the overall trend but does not state individual values.

untested.parts: Language, chess and reward-modelling settings; only linear-probe vision classification is tested.
Auxiliary confidence loss, loss variants, bootstrapping; only hierarchical co-supervision and consistency-based denoising are tested.
Student size sweep, non-vision tasks, and representation-based predictors of PGR. Only weak-supervisor capability (training iterations) is swept.

missing.what: Statement that DomainNet 'poses greater challenges for the prior method': vanilla PGR is lower than on ImageNet (axis 35–65% vs 55–80%), a task dependence.
Statement that the gain from 2 to 6 supervisors is particularly large with noise reduction.
Numeric PGR values per supervisor accuracy in the Figure 2 sweep (axes 0–70% PGR, 0–0.5 supervisor accuracy).

record.verdict_notes: The record's rows r2–r29 attach V1 and V3 to every method condition and give the 1-supervisor 'All' rows the vanilla baseline as their own baseline. Those rows are the baseline. Number of supervisors is a V2 method parameter, not a V3 size/task variable. The V3 label was changed from limits_scope to supports: PGR depending on the capability gap is exactly what V3 describes. Baseline PGR being above 0 is inferred from figure axis ranges in the extracted text, not from stated numbers. T1 is kept because the baseline replicates the original vision protocol; the method comparison alone would be T2.

versions.untested_parts: The reported tests are visual classification with linear classifiers; language and other task settings are not tested.
Tests co-supervision and denoising, not auxiliary confidence loss, alternative loss variants, or other proposed training changes.
Varies supervisor capability and the number of specialized supervisors across two vision datasets. It does not sweep student model size or compare representations as predictors.
No test of distribution shift, exploitable errors beyond a supervisor's checking ability, or correlated weak- and strong-model errors.
No theoretical conditions for a student to beat its supervisor are tested or derived.
Tests visual recognition only; no other non-language modalities are tested.
